item.title: Stephen A. Smith says Giants HC John Harbaugh ‘should be ashamed’ after what he’s just heard
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images The New York Giants suffered a substantial defeat on Thursday night against their NFC East rivals, the Washington Commanders, in the race for the division. Although the Giants will end this week’s round of games still at the top of the NFC East, the game at MetLife Stadium should be viewed as a massive missed opportunity to take control of the division. Instead, the Giants have left the door open for the Dallas Cowboys to close the gap at the top. John Harbaugh was brought to the Giants in the offseason to help the Giants in the NFC East, but Thursday night’s game showed signs of the old Giants from years gone by. Stephen A. Smith was left far from impressed with what he saw at MetLife Stadium, and he took his frustration out on the veteran head coach. Stephen A. Smith unleashes on New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh Fortunately for the Giants , the Cowboys will be facing the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, but an unexpected victory could galvanise Brian Schottenheimer’s team heading into the final months of the season. “I mean, John Harbaugh should be ashamed of himself. That’s really what this is,” Smith said on First Take. “The point that I’m making is this: John Harbaugh, this is not new. This is one of the problems that existed in Baltimore, in terms of being a bit outdated. Coming across as a bit, okay, of course he knows what he’s doing in terms of being a football coach overall. Of course he knows how to lead. He’s been there forever, he’s been in the NFL, we understand and have nothing but profound respect, he’s a Super Bowl champion, we get all of that. “But on too many occasions, you’re coaching scared. Which is why, what is the number, Shay, right now? 47 fourth-quarter blown leads in his career over the last decade-plus? I mean, that’s just embarrassing.” The statistic shared by Smith certainly does not reflect well on Harbaugh. The Giants have brought in a former Super Bowl winner, but he clearly has a track record of blowing the lead in the fourth quarter. Something worth keeping in mind is the Giants’ run of fixtures following what should have been a comfortable win over a struggling Commanders team. Before the end of the season, the Giants still have to play Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland, Detroit and Dallas. Granted, the Giants still hold the lead in the division, but the game on Thursday was an almost-certain victory that they have thrown away. Perhaps Harbaugh and the Giants were looking beyond Thursday’s game at some of the more difficult tests coming up over the coming weeks. It has certainly come back to bite them. item.title: Big stadiums v small stadiums - which is better?
item.description: [BBC] Each week we ask you for your opinions on one of the pressing topics concerning the Women's Super League. This time we are asking for your thoughts on clubs playing their matches in large grounds used by the men's sides. Is it better for women to play in big stadiums with empty seats or smaller stadiums where facilities are sometimes below par, but maybe where the more compact nature and smaller capacity makes for a better atmosphere? All of Chelsea's WSL games this season take place at Stamford Bridge after moving on from Kingsmeadow, while Arsenal have made Emirates Stadium their home having previously staged games at Borehamwood. Chelsea entertain WSL leaders Manchester City on Saturday, but the Blues had less than 6,000 watching at home against Everton last week. Arsenal have the highest attendance figures in the league, however their best attended league match in 2026-27, which saw 29,853 watch their game with Manchester United, was still played out at a half-empty Emirates. There are no men's matches this weekend, but Manchester United, Tottenham and West Ham are not hosting their WSL games at the men's sides stadiums, with United instead at Leigh, Tottenham at Leyton Orient and West Ham at Dagenham and Redbridge. However, the Aston Villa v Birmingham derby is at Villa Park and Brighton versus Liverpool is at American Express Stadium. What can be done to boost WSL attendances and atmospheres? item.title: Mercedes and Audi unveil adidas collections for F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes and Audi have unveiled special adidas fan collections for the upcoming Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Mercedes' range is called "Neon Lights", while Audi's is named "After Hours". Both collections are available now through adidas.com, and the pieces listed on the brand's US store range in price from $30 to $200. The most expensive items are the outerwear. Mercedes' Las Vegas jacket and Audi's Las Vegas bomber jacket both cost $200. The Mercedes collection is the bigger of the two. Alongside the jacket, it includes a $120 hoodie, a $95 long-sleeve T-shirt, $60 shorts, a $55 driver cap, a $50 race cap and T-shirts at $40 and $45. Audi's line-up has a $55 driver cap, two graphic T-shirts at $45 each and a $30 bag. The table’s open, and the adidas Las Vegas collection is ready to play. ♠️ Shop now: https://t.co/XPXZadBZQN https://t.co/XSwaPXAnoI — Audi Revolut F1 Team (@audif1_) November 12, 2026 The two teams arrive in Las Vegas in very different positions. Mercedes secured the 2026 constructors' championship at the Brazilian Grand Prix. Audi, in its first season as a works team after taking over Sauber, currently sits eighth in the standings with 28 points. The German outfit is three points behind Haas. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli claimed the drivers' title at the Mexican Grand Prix, becoming the youngest champion in the history of F1. His team-mate George Russell is currently in the fight for second in the championship, sitting third behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen . Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg currently sit 14th and 15th in the drivers' standings, both on 14 points. The Las Vegas Grand Prix takes place from 19 to 21 November and is the first of the final three rounds of the season, ahead of Qatar and Abu Dhabi. item.title: Arsenal defender scores international brace playing out of position
item.description: Arsenal defender scores international brace playing out of position Jurrien Timber starred for the Netherlands playing at left-back on Friday night, scoring a brace in a win over Greece and Arsenal teammate Christos Tzolis. Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images Arsenal teammates Jurrien Timber and Christos Tzolis faced off with their national teams on Friday, with the Netherlands taking on Greece in the Nations League. The two teams had made unbeaten starts to the group stage, winning two games and drawing two games each. But any hopes of a close contest were quickly extinguished by a dominant Netherlands display. Timber found himself playing at left-back, rather than his usual positions on the right or at centre-back. But he was still heavily involved in a free-scoring first half. Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images Timber played the pass before the goal for the Netherlands’ second and third goals of the half, which both came in the opening 20 minutes of the game. The Arsenal defender then scored a striker’s finish from close range in the 40th minute, to make it 5-0. But the goals didn’t stop at half-time, and Timber popped up at the back post for another tap-in for 6-0 in the 59th minute. With the Netherlands going on to score a seventh two minutes later, the game slowed down. The two teams made nine substitutions between them in the following 15 minutes, including the withdrawals of both Timber and Tzolis. The highlights are available here . From an Arsenal point of view, considering the two players have been injured recently, it was good to see neither had to complete the full 90. Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images Greece may have suffered a damaging blow to their confidence, but they still have a chance to progress to the knockouts. If they better Germany’s result in the final games, they’ll make the Nations League quarter-finals. The same is true if both teams draw or both lose. But if they both win, Germany will go through. Greece host Serbia on Monday, November 16th, 19:45 GMT, whilst Germany host the Netherlands at the same time. Greece will have to hope the Netherlands are just as ruthless against Germany. item.title: Refusing to Buy Defensive Cover in January Would Be Negligence That Will Cost Manchester City the Title
item.description: Refusing to Buy Defensive Cover in January Would Be Negligence That Will Cost Manchester City the Title Hugo Viana and co must strengthen Manchester City's backline in January. Since a 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad Stadium in October, players such as Marc Guehi, Gianluigi Donnarumma and Josko Gvardiol have struggled immensely, be it because of a lack of confidence or the concerning selection choices that Maresca is making far too often. The 46-year-old, having started life as Pep Guardiola’s successor perfectly with eight consecutive wins, has been subjected to intense scrutiny ahead of the November international break, mainly because of his tactical structure against Nottingham Forest . City lost 3-1 after Liam Delap twice capitalised on poor defending following Jair Cunha’s opening goal just six minutes into the contest at the City Ground. All three goals came from errors that were caused by Maresca’s decision to leave Elliot Anderson stranded deep in midfield, and at the same time, Enzo Fernandez was ordered to play higher up, in closer proximity to Rayan Cherki. It was a game in agonising need for someone like Ayyoub Bouaddi. The defeat was humbling in that Forest, who hadn’t scored a goal at home for 167 days, managed to claim victory and pile vast confusion amongst City supporters, who saw their side drop into third in the Premier League table behind leaders Arsenal and second-placed Brighton and Hove Albion . A drop in form has drawn a scroll of questions that need to be answered in the coming weeks if Maresca wants to regain belief in his side, and so too to receive backing from Manchester City supporters. So what’s the fix? Even in their struggles to put the ball into the back of the net at the top of the pitch, it’s clear that the main focus in the January transfer window for sporting director Hugo Viana and Maresca must be defenders. Shortly after completing the signing of Fernandez for a joint-British record fee of £125 million from Chelsea , Maresca said that the Argentine is “unbelievable around the box” , and it seems the Italian wants to play him higher up the pitch. This theory has led to reasonable anger as to why Maresca insists on playing him alongside Anderson in midfield, who, despite his unbelievable talent and work rate, simply cannot keep up with one, two, or three players attacking his box at once. These leaky defensive performances won’t fix themselves, but it would be naive to predict that Maresca is too stubborn to change his ways. The manager has found success at Leicester City and Chelsea, and will want to mirror that on a large scale, perhaps, in east Manchester. In some ways, Maresca needs to look at the 2024-25 season under Guardiola to realise that splashing big money on defenders may be more of a necessity than it is a desire. item.title: Maryland volleyball outlasted by Rutgers in five-set loss
item.description: Through 16 matches of Big Ten play, Maryland women’s volleyball’s attacking errors in tight sets have been the primary hurdle they’ve been unable to overcome versus conference competition. Against Rutgers on Friday night, that proved to be true once again. Despite out-killing the Scarlet Knights, 72-64, behind 65 assists from Sara Toth, Maryland lost 31 points on attack errors in a heartbreaking 3-2 road loss. Coming off a clean sweep defeat against Penn State on Wednesday, Maryland went into this match ready to defend its position in the Big Ten tournament. Maryland entered the game in 15th place, the last seed in the tournament, while the Scarlet Knights stood at 16th The teams knew it was an important night for them both, having come into this match struggling at 3-12 in the conference. The Terps established momentum by drawing the first blood of the night with a kill from star freshman Brooklynne Brass. Maryland continued to protect its lead in short, sporadic bursts as the set went on. Even as the set remained close, the Terps emerged with a .184 hitting percentage and took home the opening frame of the night, 26-24. Despite dropping the opening set, the Scarlet Knights restored their momentum just in time for the second set. In another thrilling set, both defenses went toe-to-toe, as seen by the close hitting percentages in this set. Even after Maryland built a 15-10 lead at the media timeout, three Terps service errors and a late 4-0 Scarlet Knights run allowed Rutgers to seal the frame, 25-22. In the third set, Rutgers won by the exact same score. It took a lead at 7-6 and didn’t trail after that, with the Terps putting up a meager .140 hitting percentage. The fourth set continued the neck-in-neck battle. After taking two consecutive sets, Rutgers wanted to carry its momentum into another successive set, but Maryland stayed relentless in its attempts to hang on. With a total of six ties, the set proved to be yet another close matchup for both teams. The Terps managed their way through a significant 5-1 run mid-set, a stretch that would remain consequential for their inevitable win. As hard as they tried, Rutgers couldn’t overcome that deficit — allowing Maryland to take their second set at 25-20. That victory propelled both teams into the ultimate five-set thriller. Unfazed by their most recent set loss, the Scarlet Knights sparked an immediate 4-1 burst.. But another kill from Brass took the Terps to their first lead of the fifth set. Yet, that hope was short-lived. With a kill from outside hitter Karis Willow, who spent the match executing at .333 clearance, Rutgers took home a final close set at 15-13 and won the match. item.title: Rayan hands Manchester United open transfer invitation after making bold personal admission
item.description: Rayan hands Manchester United open transfer invitation after making bold personal admission What AFC Bournemouth’s Rayan has just confessed about the Cherries’ 3-0 win over Manchester United should set alarm bells ringing at Old Trafford. Last month, the Cherries travelled to Manchester and outwitted Michael Carrick ’s side, a statement victory that added to the misery of the embattled former United head coach. Weeks later, that win is still being discussed. In an interview alongside clubmate Evanilson for ESPN Brazil , as transcribed by Sport Witness , Rayan was asked how it felt to beat United. Rayan’s Manchester United confession He replied while making some interesting confessions: “Yeah, it’s true, that’s exactly how it feels. I was even talking to the people at home, my wife and the people who are with me, and I told them I’ve always supported Manchester United here in England.” The interviewer then asked whether, while still a Bournemouth player, he continues to follow United. “Yes, really,” he answered. When pressed on why, he added: “Because of Cristiano Ronaldo.” Rayan could have been a Manchester United player Hearing Rayan say this, and remembering that United could reportedly have signed him last winter ahead of Bournemouth, will frustrate Old Trafford supporters. But what has frustrated them further is how quickly he adapted to the Premier League. Rayan Premier League stats He arrived and immediately transferred his Vasco da Gama goalscoring form, finding the net five times in his first 15 games while providing two assists. His bright start prompted leading outlets to produce detailed analysis of his quality. The Athletic labelled him “already one of the Premier League’s most fearsome attackers”. The piece highlighted how perfectly he filled the void left by Antoine Semenyo, noting how decisive the now Manchester City forward had been for the Cherries. Big transfer boost All of this gives United perfect motivation to bring Rayan to Old Trafford. Should they find themselves in a race for his signature, he is likely to lean towards a move to M16. Favouring a switch to Manchester is one thing, however; meeting Bournemouth’s hefty asking price is quite another. The versatile Bournemouth star reportedly carries a £130 million release clause in his deal at the Vitality Stadium.

(Photo by Grace Hoppel/MLB Photos via Getty Images) MLB Photos via Getty Images The Los Angeles Dodgers have wasted little time getting their offseason roster work underway following another season at the top of the National League, but with a disappointing finish before the World Series. As the general manager meetings began this week in Las Vegas, the Dodgers announced an initial move, acquiring a player who appeared to be a promising piece of the Philadelphia Phillies’ future before joining their division rival, then being picked up by the Dodgers. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets $22 Million Castoff Sends ‘Crazy’ Message After Surprise Trade Los Angeles Dodgers Add Former Philadelphia Phillies Infielder On Monday, the Dodgers announced they had claimed infielder Christian Cairo shortly after he left the Phillies for the New York Mets. “The Dodgers claimed IF Christian Cairo from the New York Mets,” the team stated . Cairo, 25, has yet to make his major league debut despite spending several seasons working his way through professional baseball’s minor league system. His brief Mets stay represented another change of organizations after a lengthy stint with Philadelphia. “A career-long minor-leaguer who spent most of last year in the Philadelphia Phillies’ organization –– hitting .227 with a .676 OPS in 128 games with their triple-A affiliate –– Cairo was a late-season waiver addition for the Mets, who subsequently re-signed him to a one-year contract on a split MLB/minor-league deal earlier this month,” Jack Harris reported for the New York Post . The Phillies designated Cairo for assignment in September and the Mets subsequently claimed him off waivers before eventually designating him for assignment themselves on November 2, despite the new contract. The Dodgers have now stepped in to claim the infielder, giving him another opportunity to continue his professional career with a new organization. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Cubs’ $68 Million Starter Castoff Jameson Taillon Makes Return Announcement What Christian Cairo Could Bring To Los Angeles Dodgers After Philadelphia Phillies Exit Cairo offers some positional flexibility that could make him useful as organizational depth. He has experience at second base, shortstop and third base, while also seeing action in the outfield during his minor league career. Cairo recorded 25 stolen bases in 2026 and drew more walks than strikeouts during his minor league campaign. Those abilities could give Los Angeles another versatile option to evaluate heading into spring training. item.title: FA Cup test for the Welsh side aiming for WSL 2
item.description: Gwalia United are unbeaten in nine games in all competitions but face a stern challenge this weekend [Benjamin Brain Photography] For a club with ambitions of reaching the Women's Super League's second tier (WSL 2) by 2030, Gwalia United's relegation last season to the fourth tier of English women's football looks a significant setback. Yet there is a belief at the Welsh club that taking one step in the wrong direction can ultimately help take them forward. This Sunday (14:00 GMT) brings the chance for Gwalia to show they are making progress once more, as they target an upset against Oxford United in the Women's FA Cup second round. The U's are top of the division Gwalia dropped out of last season, and so are within sight of WSL 2. In short, they are where Gwalia want to be, and will start as favourites to seal a round-three place at USW Sport Park. Yet for Gwalia, the cup brings a chance for what would be a statement victory. "It takes a lot of pressure off us because people from the outside looking in probably don't expect us to do a lot," says captain Cerys Jones "It's a good opportunity to challenge ourselves." Relegation 'hit us hard' Gwalia will have beaten AFC Stoneham and Yate Town in this season's Women's FA Cup [Benjamin Brain Photography] Gwalia, who were formerly known as Cardiff City Ladies, have a proud history of developing Welsh talent. Stars such as Jess Fishlock, Sophie Ingle, Ffion Morgan, Gemma Evans and Lily Woodham played for the club before going on to represent Wales. And after co-owners Julian Jenkins and Canva founder Damien Singh got involved before the 2024-25 season, there was hope of keeping some of that emerging talent within Wales while allowing Gwalia to compete at a higher level. However, making progress has not been easy, even if last season's relegation from the Southern Premier Division was the result of fine margins. Gwalia finished with the same goal difference as AFC Wimbledon, but were relegated as the London club had scored one more goal. "It hit us hard, it really did," says manager Cori Williams-Mills. Gwalia are currently fourth in Division One South West, having lost only one of their eight league games so far this season. The average age of the squad is just 20, and Williams-Mills believes her youthful team can not only return to the third tier but go on to reach new heights. "When we get back up, we'll be better equipped than we would have been if we'd stayed [up]," she adds. "Sometimes taking a step back can help push you further forward. "We ended last year a little disappointed. This season, the girls have been excellent. "Is it going to take us time to get where we want to be? Is it going to be hard along the way? Yeah, of course it is, but we'll get there." item.title: Mancini has three key Italy line-up doubts for Belgium clash as Cambiaghi trains separately
item.description: Mancini has three key Italy line-up doubts for Belgium clash as Cambiaghi trains separately Sky Sport Italia reports that Nicolò Cambiaghi trained separately this morning, so Federico Dimarco could replace him against Belgium, but coach Roberto Mancini has two more line-up doubts. Italy visit Belgium on Sunday for the final Nations League group-stage game. The Azzurri are currently the Group A1 leaders, level on 10 points with France, but with a better head-to-head record. Belgium sit third with nine points, while Turkiye have already been relegated to the second division, with five defeats from five. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) Italy trained at the Inter training centre this morning, before flying to Brussels in the afternoon. Sky Sport reports that Cambiaghi trained separately, so if he’s not fit enough to start, or even be available tomorrow, Dimarco will feature in the Azzurri XI instead as a left winger. Mancini’s other doubt is on the right flank, with either Vergara or Sebastiano Esposito starting. According to Sky, Vergara is the slight favourite after his convincing performance against France on Thursday, when the Napoli talent earned the second penalty kick of the night. Coach Roberto Mancini during an Italy training session (@azzurri) There’s also uncertainty over one of the three central midfielders. item.title: Keith Cooper Jr. Returns To Dolphins As Roster Spot Opens
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins moved quickly on Wednesday to fill a gap in their lineup. The team signed defensive lineman Keith Cooper Jr. off the Carolina Panthers practice squad, according to Dolphins Wire . This move fills one of three open spots created earlier in the week. They also waived cornerback Reese Taylor to clear the necessary space. Cooper is not a stranger to the organization. He played for Miami during the offseason before making the final roster out of camp. He was waived by the team in late September and fully released in early October. item.description: Kirk Herbstreit gives some love to his dog, Peter. © USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Kirk Herbstreit’s recent outing with his dog Peter has sparked controversy. The ESPN college football analyst shared a video of his dog enjoying a steak at a New York City restaurant. While the moment seemed cute to Herbstreit, sports commentator Craig Carton was not happy about it. He questioned the decision to bring a dog into a steakhouse and feed it a meal meant for humans. Herbstreit posted a video of himself cutting a steak and placing the pieces in front of Peter. The golden retriever wasted no time in finishing the meal, eating an entire plate of cut-up steak in less than 17 seconds. “Petey got into another steak in NYC last night… I wish he would enjoy it,” Herbstreit wrote. However, Carton reacted very differently when discussing the video on his show. “I’m not anti-dog. I just don’t want to go to a steakhouse and eat next to a dog. Because it’s disgusting,” Carton said. He went on to criticize Herbstreit for documenting the experience and questioned why the analyst would serve an expensive steak to his dog while dining with his wife and friends. “‘I love my dog more than you love your dog. You look to your right, and a beautifully cooked medium-rare steak is delivered to the Herbstreit table, but it’s not for any of the adults at that table, it’s for his dog. And Kirk, on camera now, because you’ve got to document everything you do, God forbid you act like a human being and you don’t film every aspect of your life – in a New York City steakhouse,” he added. According to Carton, other customers expecting a quiet meal may have been disturbed by a dog sitting next to them. Kirk Herbstreit’s Dog Peter Continues Ben’s Legacy Peter always accompanies Herbstreit during his college football travels. The golden retriever took on that role after the analyst lost his previous dog, Ben, in November 2024. He spread his love across the country and so many of you welcomed him into your lives. We miss him every day and are so appreciative of his spirit that blessed so many lives for the 10 years he was alive. Love you Benny,” Herbstreit wrote. The tribute received an outpouring of affection from fans. Many remembered Ben fondly, while others showered the dog with praise. item.title: Jamal Mashburn: “That’s not Kentucky Basketball”
item.description: Big Blue Nation hasn’t been afraid to let their voices be heard following Kentucky Basketball ’s narrow win against Northern Arizona on Friday night. Obviously, barely beating a team you should’ve handled easily, and were over a 30-point favorite against, isn’t acceptable at Kentucky. It’s especially not acceptable when it comes on the heels of an extremely embarrassing loss in Chicago against Kansas only a few nights before. Well, along with Big Blue Nation, and frankly, it feels like every college basketball fan, a special media member chimed in on the state of the Kentucky Basketball program Tuesday night. Kentucky legend Jamal Mashburn made some comments on TNT later in the evening. “I think most people in Big Blue Nation are very disappointed at this particular time. They take their basketball very seriously,” Mashburn said. “It just seems like this particular team, or I would say over the last couple of years with Pope’s teams, they’ll do something well and then the next game they won’t do it well. There seems to be a lot of inconsistency. They have trouble guarding the basketball. Northern Arizona shot over 50% from three and also from two.” Mash is calling it like it is; this team hasn’t played even close to good enough defense. Teams have been lining it up and drilling threes like it’s a shootaround because of too much gambling, not enough effort, offensive rebounds, or a mix of all. He did give one of very, very few positives from the night, saying, “They moved the basketball today. 21 assists and just four turnovers.” “This is going to be a long road, and I think a lot of people are going to start asking the bigger question: ‘What does Mark Pope’s future look like?’ I think that’s the elephant in the room,” Mashburn stated. “It’s sad. I’m a Kentucky fan and obviously played there. I want to see them do well; it just doesn’t seem like it’s clicking.” Mashburn continued, “To win against Northern Arizona on a buzzer-beater almost…that’s not Kentucky Basketball, and that’s not championship basketball.” “The only person that I’ve known that’s been able to take role players and kind of blend them together, and a lot of people don’t give him the respect he deserves, is Tubby Smith — but Mark Pope is not Tubby Smith.” Well, we’ve now heard one of the Wildcat greats give his thoughts on it, and he said it best: this is not Kentucky Basketball. item.description: Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak and Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins. Kirk Cousins’ sudden departure from the Las Vegas Raiders has raised questions about who really made the call to move him. The Raiders had been building their offense around the veteran quarterback, and coach Klint Kubiak had publicly defended him just days before the trade deadline. Yet Cousins has now returned to the Minnesota Vikings, prompting Shannon Sharpe and Chad Johnson to question how much say Kubiak had in the decision. Shannon Sharpe and Chad Johnson Question Klint Kubiak’s Role in Kirk Cousins Trade Discussing the move on the “Nightcap” podcast, Sharpe and Johnson said they believe Kubiak had precious little involvement in the Raiders’ decision to send Cousins to Minnesota. Minnesota sent its own 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas at the trade deadline and assumed approximately $650,000 in remaining 2026 base salary, along with a $10 million roster bonus due in March 2027. Johnson pointed to the power structure in NFL front offices, arguing that head coaches do not always control major personnel decisions. “He (John Spytek) made the decision. Klint ain’t had nothing to do with that,” Johnson said. Sharpe agreed, adding that only certain established coaches have enough authority to influence major roster moves. He mentioned Mike Tomlin, Sean Payton, Andy Reid and Bill Belichick as examples of coaches who would have a say in a decision involving a starting quarterback. Kubiak’s subdued demeanor during the joint press conference contrasted with Spytek’s more animated presentation, prompting speculation about whether the coach supported the trade. Kubiak and Cousins had worked together in Minnesota before reuniting in Las Vegas. Kubiak served as Cousins’ quarterbacks coach from 2019-20 and offensive coordinator in 2021. item.title: “The desire is there on all sides” – Thioune hopeful of permanent Füllkrug deal as West Ham hold the key
item.description: “The desire is there on all sides” – Thioune hopeful of permanent Füllkrug deal as West Ham hold the key Werder Bremen coach Daniel Thioune has made it clear that the Bundesliga side want to keep Niclas Füllkrug beyond the end of his loan spell from West Ham, which expires in the summer. However, Thioune also pointed to the financial considerations and the role of Füllkrug's parent club. “I think the desire is there on all sides," Thioune told Transfermarkt. "He doesn't feel under pressure to prove himself; rather, he is eager to show what he can do. Of course, it then becomes a question of what West Ham want and what they are willing and able to do. And we have to be equally honest about our own situation: What are we capable of, and what is Niclas willing to do? "But we, as a club, I as a coach, and Niclas himself are all very interested in continuing to work together beyond the summer.” Bremen managing director Klaus Filbry recently expressed the club's hopes of retaining the striker as well. “Of course, West Ham are an important third party in this situation. The league Werder are playing in at the end of the season will also play a role. Nevertheless, I remain cautiously optimistic that we can ultimately make the deal happen,” Filbry told Bild.
